text:
opsbot: ALERT: [prod-us-west] GPU error rate spike detected (12x) since 03:04 UTC after driver rollout. Sample: "NVRM: Xid (0x9e)" and increased NCCL watchdog timeouts. Alert: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/12345

maria: :eyes: which pool/cluster is affected?

opsbot: affected: inference-pool-usw2-a (mixed A40/RTX). 19/120 nodes showing errors. rollout tag: driver-v2.3.0-canary finished ~03:00 UTC.

aj: do we have a rollback plan? can we evict traffic first?

cheng: quick triage steps: ssh one node, run `dmesg | tail -n50` and `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n200`, check kernel vs driver versions.

leo: grabbing logs from inf-prod-usw2-a-047 now.

leo: paste: "NVRM: Xid (0x8c) 144 00:..." and repeated "NCCL WARN Watchdog detected stall" entries in /var/log/messages.

samir: pattern looks like the last regression we saw when kernel module ABI mismatched after a driver bump.

evan: note: some nodes still on kernel 5.15.12 while the driver was built/tested on 5.19.x — DKMS may not have rebuilt on those hosts.

maria: if kernel/driver mismatch suspected, options: rebuild DKMS on nodes, or rollback driver to v2.2.x. Rebuild is lower blast but slower.

aj: rollback command (canary first): `deploy-bot rollback-driver --pool inference-pool-usw2-a --to v2.2.1 --parallel 5` — will cordon+drain nodes, takes ~8-12m per batch.

cheng: runbook TL;DR (paste):
```
# quick mitigation
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
deploy-bot rollback-driver --node <node> --to v2.2.1
systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced || modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia
verify: dmesg/journal, prometheus: nvidia_driver_errors, nccl_watchdog_count
```

maria: also enable temporary autoscale to shift traffic to eu/us-east while we stabilize. I'll open an autoscale task.

samir: I'll spin up a 5-node canary with v2.2.1 and run the same workload for 30m.

leo: monitoring: I'll add a temporary alert rule to suppress noisy auto-remediations and track NCCL latency percentiles.

opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-0345. Runbook link: https://go.redwood/runbooks/gpu-driver-regression. Assigned: samir, leo, cheng.

maria: thanks — keep updates here. If rollback succeeds, schedule postmortem and add kernel-driver compatibility checks into the upgrade pipeline. :thumbsup:
